features.feature: `assert` decides a proposition with the outcomes true, false, unknown and error; only true commits the cell; a false or unknown assertion fails it
A bare proposition displays its truth value (`gcd(84, 30) = 6` gives true; false is a successful cell; unknown displays)
`and` conjoins assertions, commits once, and names the failed conjunct
Definitions: `let x := e in D` with a checked ascription, `let p(x) := e in D` with an indeterminate binder, bare `NAME := expr [in D]`, and `let x: T := e in C` with both ascriptions
Reserved notation: `e` (Euler's number) and `i` (imaginary unit) cannot be rebound; `d` and `π` are constants a binding may shadow; `--` begins a comment
features.note: No requirement states the reservation; FR-002 and FR-008 cover the meaning of i and e.

features.feature: Spelling aliases: NN ZZ QQ RR R CC, the backslash family (\NN \in \leq \mapsto), |-> and \mapsto for ↦, -> for →, `is` for =, `in` for ∈, Mod(QQ) and QQ-Mod, QQ^3 for ℚ³, 2^ℤ for 𝒫(ℤ)
features.note: The catalogue `notations` fields own the kernel spellings; the workloads keep `is` (several_variables.dimension).

features.feature: Precedence: a superscript binds tighter than the implicit product (`3x²` is `3·(x²)`); unary minus stays out of it; the braced exponent `x^{k}`; a parenthesized receiver `(360).factor()`; the prefix spelling `gcd(84, 30)` of a method
Binder scope: comprehension, function and ∑ binders are local and publish nothing; a binding wins over the indeterminate and over the prefix-method reading

LaTeX-first display: each result emits one bundle with text/latex (inline, ASCII math mode) and text/plain; no text/latex where a value has no natural form (truth values, non-ASCII binders, the ℤ/4 module); assertions and diagnostics stay textual

Display conventions: rational coefficients `(1/2)x^2`; a series by its rule ends in `…` and a truncation in `O(t^n)`; a vector is the tuple `(1, 2)`; a span shows its reduced basis and its ambient space; a product and a power set are denoted, not listed; a 1-form shows `dx`
A value payload `application/vnd.casdsl.value+json` beside the display (a multiset, a progression, an approximation with its exact source; a denoted set has none)

Choice disclosures in notation on the result they qualify: the branch cut of the `√` spelling, the fixed embedding $\bar{\mathbb{Q}} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$ of the roots and factors in $\mathbb{C}[x]$
Advisory notes on results, for example `p does not split over ℤ: it has 1 of its 3 roots there (with multiplicity)`
`#explain_route`: the inheritance path as a chain of maps, the Mathlib anchor of the operation, the backend routine and its documentation link, in mathematical wording
`#capabilities`: each method with its declaring category, anchor and implemented routes
`#capability_gaps`: methods that are available and have no implementation for a presentation
`#canonical_maps`: the registered identifications that drive ⊆, ∈, `map … to` and coercion, each with its documentation; a defective (two-way or doubled) registration is a loud error
features.note: The kernel reads inclusions as catalogue rows (`incl.sets.*`); no requirement names a listing command.

features.feature: NoImplementation: a structured gap that names the operation, the object, the inheritance path and the routes considered; the mathematics stays available

Refusals by name: held spellings, a truncation target that is not a ring, ℝ/O(ε) that is not a quotient, a morphism ascribed as an object, a lambda without ascription, domains that do not compose, an argument outside the domain, a shape mismatch of matrix and vector, a symbolic body at a point

Approximation semantics: the exact source is kept; the requested and the achieved tolerances travel with the decimal; $\varepsilon$ must be a positive rational; an unmeetable $\varepsilon$ is a capability failure that names it; no arithmetic on approximations; two approximations compare as unknown; the decimal is checked against its bound
Bare `=` is bound to one category: `F = {0, 1, 2, 3}` is false for the module `F`; the set question is `set_eq` through the underlying set
Methods inherited along category inclusions and transported along a preferred forgetful functor (`UnderlyingSet` from modules to sets); two applicable routes are an ambiguity, not a choice
One arithmetic: ∑ and ∏ fold the same + and × that the binary operators use, attached to the structure of the elements
Mathlib anchors: each category and method names its Mathlib meaning; registered memberships and inclusions must be discharged by Mathlib; availability is checked against Mathlib at each call
features.note: The kernel takes this authority from lean-categories, not from checks in the kernel.

features.feature: A contributed term production with its translator (`tripleof x` is 3·x) extends the surface without an edit to the core grammar
Executors keyed by (backend, operation); operation signatures checked when a route registers; a nullary operation refuses an argument

The wire codec rejects malformed frames (bad magnitude, zero denominator, a shape that contradicts its size, an unknown tag, a symbol outside the vocabulary); the Sage adapter announces its capabilities and answers an unknown operation as unsupported
Replies checked against the request: factorizations multiplied back, roots evaluated, charpoly, determinant and companion matrix checked
features.note: FR-014 gives checkers no correctness authority; the kernel now observes kernel behaviour and independent expectations assess answers.

features.feature: The notebook is a document: each output is the result of the visible prefix; an edit re-runs the cell and the cells below (↻); an upstream failure stops the run; a failed cell commits nothing
Notebook re-execution gate: stored outputs must equal a live document-order run, byte-stable, with timing metadata kept
End-to-end acceptance through the real Jupyter protocol against the installed `casdsl` kernelspec
Install of the Jupyter kernelspec (`nbdsl_kernel.install --project . --prelude-module CasDsl.Notebook --name casdsl`) and the sync-kernel recipe that restarts stale kernels
features.note: FR-094 to FR-098 cover the launch of the Sage interpreter; no requirement names the kernelspec install.

features.feature: The Sage adapter runs as a separate process started by `sage -python backends/sage_adapter.py`; a missing `sage` is a loud failure
A control notebook on a plain Python kernel
An ordinary Lean command in a cell still elaborates as Lean
Emitted prose speaks mathematics: no internal vocabulary, no issue citations in diagnostics
Plain numbers are naturally elements of $\mathbb{Z}$: a bare numeral is read in $\mathbb{Z}$ unless an ascription selects another domain
features.note: The workload readings keep this convention (assumption A1 of `workload-routes.md`).

features.feature: `d` displays the universal relative differential $d : \mathcal{O}_X \to \Omega^1_{X/S}$ and its coordinate form $\mathbb{Q}[x] \to \Omega^1_{\mathbb{Q}[x]/\mathbb{Q}} \cong \mathbb{Q}[x]\,dx$; the integral displays as a coset of the kernel of $d/dx$

missing_catalogue_rows.description: A rational approximation of a real number within a positive rational tolerance: for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, a chosen $a \in \mathbb{Q}$ with $|x - a| < \varepsilon$ (a choice-bearing operation; the chosen decimal is retained with the exact source and both tolerances).

The factorization of a nonzero element of a unique factorization domain into a unit and irreducible factors with multiplicities, for $\mathbb{Z}$ (the catalogue has it for $\mathbb{N}^{+}$ through `mor.sets.nat_prime_factors` and `mor.sets.nat_multiplicity`, and for $R[x]$ through `mor.sets.polynomial_factorization`).

Primality of an element of a commutative ring ($x$ prime when $(x)$ is a nonzero prime ideal), for $\mathbb{Z}$, so that $-7$ is prime and $0$, $1$ are not (the catalogue has `mor.sets.nat_is_prime` on $\mathbb{N}$ only).
A chosen square root in $\mathbb{C}$ of a negative rational, $\sqrt{-4} = 2i$ (the catalogue has `mor.sets.real_sqrt` on $\mathbb{R}$ only).

Exponentiation of cardinals, $2^{\kappa}$ (Mathlib `Cardinal.power`), so that $|\mathcal{P}(A)| = 2^{|A|}$ can be stated (the catalogue has the cardinal literals `lit.cardinals` and no operation on `cat.cardinals`).

The enumeration $\mathbb{N} \to X$ of a denumerable set in the adopted `Denumerable.ofNat` order ($\mathbb{Z}$: $0, -1, 1, -2, 2, \ldots$; $\mathbb{Q}$: $0, -1, -1/2, 1, 1/2, \ldots$) and its evaluation $X[k]$; objects of `cat.enumerated_sets` for $\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Q}$ and the progressions (the category and its classifier exist; no object or morphism row does).

The multiset of roots of a nonzero polynomial over a domain, with multiplicity (Mathlib `Polynomial.roots`); `mor.sets.polynomial_roots` gives the finite root set $R[x] \setminus \{0\} \to \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(R)$.
The derivation $d/dx : \mathbb{Q}[x] \to \mathbb{Q}[x]$ as a morphism of $\mathbb{Q}$-modules, so that its kernel is a subobject (`mor.sets.polynomial_derivative` is a map of sets).
The truncation $R[[t]] \to R[[t]]/(t^{n})$ (the quotient by $(t^{n})$, an $R$-algebra map) with its display $\sum_{k<n} a_k t^k + O(t^{n})$.

A linear map $\mathbb{Q}^{n} \to \mathbb{Q}^{m}$ given by a formula $(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \mapsto (\ldots)$ linear in its binders, as a morphism of `cat.modules_r` with its kernel and image (`mor.modules.row_linear_map` and `mor.modules.matrix_linear_map` take a matrix).
Objects of `cat.ideals_r` (the principal ideal $(4) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$) so that `meth.annihilator` has a value to compare with; `cat.ideals_r` has no object row.
The ℤ-module $\mathbb{Z}/4$ as an object of `cat.modules_r` (written `ℤ/4 in Modules(ℤ)`); the module rows are `obj.modules.regular`, `obj.modules.vectors` and the restricted regular module.
The inclusion $\mathbb{Q}[[t]] \subseteq \mathbb{R}[[t]]$ induced by $\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ (the catalogue inclusions are those of the number systems).
The real function $\arctan$ (the catalogue functions are `mor.sets.real_sin`, `real_cos`, `real_exp`, `real_sqrt`, `real_pi`).
The gcd of two polynomials over a UFD (`mor.sets.gcd` is the gcd of integers).
Irreducibility of a nonzero polynomial over a domain (a prime element of $R[x]$).
The cardinal $2^{\aleph_0}$ of $\mathbb{R}$ (no statement of the workloads needs an uncountable cardinal; the plan records it).
Membership in the unit group $\mathrm{Mat}_n(K)^{\times}$ as a decided predicate (the workloads read $M$ in $\mathrm{Mat}_2(\mathbb{Q})^{\times}$ as an ascription).
